title: Attribution Timeline Resolver for Per-route/Model/Customer Cost & Latency
creator: Aisha Moreno
description:
Problem: The console needs a deterministic, auditable service that computes per-route, per-model-variant, and per-customer cost and latency breakdowns at multiple time granularities (minute, hour, day) with strong freshness guarantees. Current rollups are coarse, often double-count tokens for retries and fallbacks, and lack a clear lineage for model-variant fallbacks or de-duped streaming responses.

Goal: Build an Attribution Timeline Resolver (ATR) service that ingests streaming request traces and cost probes, resolves event lineage (including retries, partial responses, streaming chunks), attributes compute and token costs to the correct route/model/customer buckets, and emits time-windowed breakdowns used by Console dashboards, chargeback, and anomaly detection. The service must: canonicalize request IDs across ingest sources, handle model-variant fallbacks (attribute to primary route with fallback tags), deduplicate streaming chunks, accommodate continuous batching accounting, and expose an explainable attribution trace for audits.

Constraints and success criteria: 1) Freshness SLO: 99% of minute-level windows available within 120s of end-of-window. 2) Determinism: given same input stream and config, outputs must be identical across deployments. 3) Scalability: support peak throughput of 25k req/s ingest with tailing bursts. 4) Backwards compatibility: minimal schema changes for Console consumers; support old rollup topics for a 2-week migration window.
acceptance_criteria: Minute/hour/day breakdown topics populated with per-route/model/customer attributes and metadata (model_variant, fallback_reason)
Deduplication removes repeated streaming chunks and retry traces (validated by synthetic bench harness)
Latency components are reported separately: queue_time, compute_time, network_time, streaming_tail
Cost split captures compute GPU-ms, tokenization tokens, and per-token kernel cost estimates
Explainability: for any aggregated row, ATR can return the canonical set of contributing request IDs and a short lineage summary via an API
Freshness: 99% of minute windows available within 120s in staging and 95% in one retained historical reprocess slot
Graceful fallback: if downstream consumer schema not ready, ATR writes compatibility topics for 14 days and supports feature-flagged consumers
implementation_notes: Ingest: subscribe to request-traces, tokenization-probes, cost-probes, and routing-decision topics. Build a read model using Kafka streams + state stores with tombstone-aware dedup keys (canonical_request_id + chunk_index)
Canonicalization: use request_id v2 (route_id + customer_id + timestamp + sequence) computed at edge; include mapping table for legacy request IDs (backfilled via batch job)
Windowing: implement sliding- and tumbling-window aggregation paths. Minute-level path optimized for low-latency commit to materialized topics; hour/day follow-up jobs for compacted archives
Model variant handling: attach primary_model_id and fallback_chain to each resolved event; by default attribute costs to primary_model_id and emit fallback metrics as separate tags
Batching & KV cache: track batch tokens and shared KV cache hits; allocate cache savings proportionally across requests in the batch using deterministic weighting (tokens_generated + tokens_prompt)
